input: This appraisal considers a proposed warehouse extension with an installed cost of $1432k, which is expected to generate net savings of $259k per year over a period of 12 years. When these savings are discounted at a discount rate of 10%, the present value of the savings amounts to $1765k. Subtracting the installed cost of $1432k from this figure gives a net present value of $333k, which is positive and therefore indicates that the project is financially attractive on the stated assumptions. It is important to note, however, that the savings figures are based on estimates provided by vendors and by the utility, and that no saving has as yet actually been measured on a comparable installation. This means that the net present value of $333k should be treated with a degree of caution, because any shortfall in the savings that are actually achieved would reduce the net present value accordingly. Overall, the appraisal shows a positive result, but the result depends heavily on estimates that have not yet been confirmed in practice on any comparable warehouse extension project.
target: The warehouse extension has a net present value of $333k at a discount rate of 10%: the present value of the expected savings, $1765k over 12 years at $259k per year, exceeds the installed cost of $1432k by that margin. The savings are vendor and utility estimates. No saving has been measured on a comparable installation, so the $333k rests on unmeasured inputs, and a shortfall in the achieved savings reduces the net present value in proportion. The cost side is an installed cost of $1432k, quoted as a single figure for the completed extension; the savings side is an estimate repeated year by year over the appraisal period, and the appraisal is only as firm as the weaker of the two. The two sides also differ in kind: the cost is committed once, at construction, while the savings accrue only if the extension performs as the vendors and the utility expect, year after year. On the stated figures the extension clears its cost of capital with the margin shown. The decision the appraisal supports is to proceed on the estimates as they stand, with the first year's measured saving as the check on the annual saving that the result assumes throughout the appraisal period.
